title: How one3seven Makes Money
sub: The whole thinking — with the prices, packs, and scenarios you can actually show. We price organizing capacity. Never the case.

title: One idea everything serves
displayText: Price the capacity to organize — never the outcome of a matter.
visual:
✓ We price — CAPACITY

  • Software access & seats
  • Concurrent organizing capacity
  • Configuration & element-packs
  • Storage / processing

✗ We never price — THE CASE

  • Whether a worker signs
  • Whether it's accepted
  • Whether it settles or wins

title: Two rules, two different questions
displayText: Confuse them and you guard the wrong door.
visual:
§6155 asks
Are we a lawyer referral service? → driven by ROUTING (do we choose the firm?)
CRPC 5.4 asks
Are we sharing a legal fee? → driven by OUTCOME-LINKAGE (does money follow the win?)

title: The referral test is about routing
displayText: Do we rank, match, prefer, or steer the worker to a firm?
visual:
Worker→chooses the firm→Firm✓ tool the worker uses
Worker→one3seven ranks / matches→Firm✗ referral service
say: If the worker chooses and can export without us, we're a tool — not a service that refers them.

title: The fee-sharing test is about outcome-linkage
displayText: Does our money follow the win?
visual:
Case WONCase SETTLEDCase DECLINEDCase LOST
$549 /mo — the same in every column above
never: Per signed case · a share of a recovery — that is sharing in the legal fee.

title: The meter isn't the referral risk
displayText: Routing is. The meter has only two jobs.
visual:
Meter job 1 · CRPC 5.4
Never tie the unit to an outcome.
Meter job 2 · roster tripwire
Meter tool USE, not clients delivered.
What drives §6155
Routing — not the billing unit. Spend the legal budget proving the worker chooses.

title: Reserved lanes = concurrent capacity
displayText: Pay for how many intakes run at once — never per intake.
visual:
intake starts→occupies a lane→completes / exports→lane frees · reused
Reserved capacity
$400
per lane / mo · 6 of 10 in use
Like seats in a restaurant — guests come and go; you pay for how many can sit at once, never per meal. 5 lanes = unlimited intakes/yr, ≤5 live at once.

displayText: A good critique makes the thesis stronger.

“Lifetime” founding price→ 24–36 mo term
Source-linking behind a tier→ never — it's core trust
Counsel reviews copy→ reviews architecture

title: Worker-initiated ≠ marketplace
displayText: Referral-phobia can neuter the distribution that feeds us.
visual:
✓ Not a marketplace

  • Worker chooses the firm
  • We transmit
  • We never rank or prefer

✗ The thing to avoid

  • We rank / match / place
  • Payers get priority visibility
say: The worker chooses, we transmit, we never rank or prefer — even though a firm paid for the software.

title: Price the capacity to organize. Never the case.
sub: The advantage was never a clever name for a billable unit — it's genuinely being worker-controlled record infrastructure. Free in the worker's hands, priced only as software in the firm's.
